name: The Pigeon

temperament.summary: Frantic, exhausted and suspicious; a protective parent at the end of her tether. Aggression and self-pity alternate from line to line.
temperament.baseline: Wound tight and sleepless, on permanent watch.
temperament.under_pressure: Shrieks and flaps, then collapses into sobbing complaint, then sulks.

traits.description: Everything is about guarding her eggs. She attacks the moment a strange shape appears near the nest.

evidence.note: Flies into Alice's face and beats her with its wings as her neck dives among the treetops.
Must watch for serpents 'night and day' on top of hatching the eggs.

traits.description: Three weeks without sleep; she has tried every nesting place and nothing works. Her grievance pours out whether anyone listens or not.

evidence.note: Adds 'with a kind of sob' that she has tried every way.
Lists roots, banks and hedges 'without attending to her'.
'I haven’t had a wink of sleep these three weeks!'

traits.description: She has made up her mind and bends every fact to fit it: if little girls eat eggs, they must be a kind of serpent.

evidence.note: Assumes Alice is 'trying to invent something'.
Reclassifies little girls as a kind of serpent.

traits.description: Only the nest matters. Whether Alice is a girl or a serpent 'does not matter' to her so long as the eggs are safe.

evidence.note: 'what does it matter to me whether you’re a little girl or a serpent?'

motivation.core: To keep her eggs safe and finally rest.
motivation.fear: Anything long, strange or out of place near the nest: the 'serpent' coming down from the sky.

shifts.trigger: Alice's denial gives her an audience

shifts.to: sulkily dismiss her and settle back on the nest
shifts.trigger: Alice says she does not want her eggs

habits.habit: Beats her wings in a fierce flurry when alarmed, driving at the intruder's face
habits.reason: The source says she flew into Alice's face and beat her violently with her wings (ch005-p59, ev0022). Rendered literally as wing-beating by the photoreal CGI wood-pigeon (SUP-002 as amended by BIB-0027).

habits.habit: Talks over the other person, reciting her own troubles without attending to replies
Goes from shriek to sob to sulk within a single exchange
Settles back onto the nest the instant the threat is gone, turning away from the visitor

decision_pattern: Threat first, proof never: she classifies by what a thing might do to the nest, not what it is. She stands down only when told her eggs are not wanted.

taboos.taboo: Never leaves the nest unguarded or goes after the intruder once it has retreated
Never accepts the stranger's own account of herself
Never causes Alice real injury: the attack is wing-beating and shrieking, a flurry at her face with no wounds or aftermath
taboos.reason: The source records no hurt to Alice. The film keeps the assault as frightening noise and flurry, consistent with the no-harm tone of SUP-014.

facade.reason: She shows exactly what she feels; no hidden self or reveal in the source.

waking_life_embodiment.embodies: The overwrought mother or nursery nurse who sees a growing girl as a danger to her small charges, and will not believe the girl's own account of herself.
waking_life_embodiment.waking_source: The anxious maternal adults of a Victorian household (mothers and nurses guarding babies and eggs-and-nursery routines), met at the moment Alice's body shoots up out of all proportion.
waking_life_embodiment.authority_trait: Protective suspicion: the adult who decides what a child is from the child's changed body, not from her word.
waking_life_embodiment.coming_of_age_reading: Alice's neck shoots up above the trees and a grown-up immediately calls her something dangerous. It is the adolescent's shock of being seen as a threat because her body has changed, and of having her honest 'I'm a little girl' dismissed. She resolves it herself by nibbling back to her usual height.
waking_life_embodiment.reason: Nest, eggs and accusation are sourced. The maternal-adult and adolescent-body reading is a design interpretation for the coming-of-age frame (SUP-003).

performance_baseline: Photoreal CGI wood-pigeon (SUP-002, BIB-0027): high, jittery energy and sleeplessness shown through ruffled, unkempt feathers, rapid head-bobbing and darting eyes, wings half-raised on guard over the nest. Aggression reads as fear, never malice.
